born.why: This code improves survival by distinguishing between critical hunger (where eating/tasting is mandatory) and routine foraging (where tasting unknowns is prioritized to expand knowledge), while using pantry counts to prevent over-carrying known safe fruits.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when starvation risk is high, learns about unknown fruits by tasting only when hunger is low to minimize harm, avoids known poisons, and distinguishes between carrying (for securing resources) and eating (for immediate energy) based on hunger levels and whether the fruit is the specific target.

The code improves safety by strictly avoiding known poisonous species, prioritizes starvation survival with high hunger thresholds, and uses a "taste" action to safely identify unknown fruits before committing to eating or carrying them, ensuring long-term foraging efficiency.

The code prioritizes survival by treating starvation risk (>85 hunger) as a reason to eat anything, uses 'taste' for unknown fruits only when safe to do so (hunger < 40) to minimize learning costs, distinguishes between carrying (for safety/pantry storage) and eating (immediate relief), and leverages the diary to avoid known poisons while actively exploring unknown species when not critically starving.

This code prioritizes immediate starvation avoidance over caching, uses trait-based pattern recognition (smell/color) to generalize poison knowledge rather than relying solely on species keys, and restricts tasting of unknown fruits to low-hunger states to prevent fatal poisoning before finding a safe food source.

The code improves by strictly separating "learning" (tasting unknowns only when safe from starvation) from "survival" (eating when critical), and prioritizing carrying known-safe foods to the pantry to reduce future foraging effort, while maintaining deterministic logic based on hunger thresholds and diary history.
